channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioural therapy reduces pain in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain: a multicentre randomised controlled trial.
item.description: An 8-week smartphone-based digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioral therapy reduced usual knee pain by 12.5 mm (95% CI -17.1 to -7.8) at 8 weeks compared to education and exercise instruction in 216 patients with chronic patellofemoral pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The effect of multimodal sensory therapy in consciousness improvement in patients with acquired brain injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 studies (884 participants) found that multimodal sensory therapy significantly improved consciousness levels (SMD, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.04-1.92) and increased the odds of coma emergence (OR, 9.85; 95% CI, 3.86-25.01) in adults with acquired brain injury-related disorders of consciousness.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Novel Telerehabilitation Interventions for Stress Urinary Incontinence : A Systematic Review of Randomised Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review of 13 RCTs found telerehabilitation-delivered pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) for stress urinary incontinence (SUI) to be safe, feasible, and effective, with comparable clinical outcomes and higher adherence versus passive controls, and comparable efficacy to conventional care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of a multicomponent exercise programme including high-intensity interval training in institutionalised older adults with probable sarcopenia: a multicentre randomised controlled trial
item.description: A 12-week multicomponent exercise program including high-intensity interval training (HIIT) significantly improved handgrip strength (mean difference: 9.11 [7.70 to 10.51]) and physical performance (SPPB mean difference: 3.75 [2.93 to 4.56]) in 92 institutionalized older adults with probable sarcopenia, with NNT of 2 for both.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Effect of Sequential Electroacupuncture Combined With Augmented Reality Gait Training on Walking Function and Neuromuscular Control in Subacute Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A single-blind RCT of 40 subacute stroke patients found sequential electroacupuncture (EA) plus augmented reality (AR) gait training improved gait speed (primary outcome) and other functional measures significantly more than AR alone over 4 weeks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Proximal and Distal Bimanual Motor Skill Learning After Stroke: Impairments, Trajectories, and Clinical Contributors
item.description: A randomized trial with 97 (sub)acute stroke patients found improvements in accuracy and coordination on both distal and proximal bimanual tasks over three days, though less than healthy individuals. Most patients with mild-to-moderate impairment exhibited substantial residual bimanual motor learning capacity early after stroke, with baseline motor and attentional impairments predicting outcomes.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Fall-prevention education after achieving independent walking is associated with reduced subsequent fall risk in patients with stroke: a retrospective pre-post intervention study.
item.description: A retrospective pre-post intervention study (n=1,437 stroke patients) found that standardized fall-prevention education delivered after achieving independent walking was associated with a lower adjusted hazard of the first fall (aHR: 0.58, 95% CI: 0.43-0.76, P<.001) and a lower fall incidence rate (IRR: 0.68, 95% CI: 0.51-0.90, P=.006).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of ankle-foot orthosis-related conditions on muscle activity, spasticity, and psychosocial outcomes after stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 studies (931 participants) found that ankle-foot orthosis (AFO)-related conditions were associated with reduced lower-limb EMG activity (SMD = -0.40) and spasticity (SMD = -0.41) after stroke, but showed no significant effect on psychosocial outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Biological effects of technique-specific manual therapy in healthy individuals and people with musculoskeletal disorders: a systematic review with meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 50 studies (2,147 participants) found that manual therapy induces short-term neurophysiological modulation with technique-specific responses. Joint mobilization significantly increased skin conductance (sympathetic marker) versus sham in healthy cohorts, while non-HVLA soft tissue techniques were associated with reduced heart rate and increased RMSSD (parasympathetic marker).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Is therapeutic exercise as a standalone intervention effective in reducing kinesiophobia in adults with nonspecific chronic low back pain? A systematic review and meta-analysis with meta-regression
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found that therapeutic exercise as a standalone intervention is effective in reducing kinesiophobia in adults with nonspecific chronic low back pain.
item.author: Eur Spine J

item.title: Home-based digital exercise versus hospital physiotherapy for plantar fasciitis: a propensity-score-matched retrospective cohort study with dual-perspective cost-utility evaluation.
item.description: A propensity-score-matched retrospective cohort study (N=587) in China found a 12-week home-based digital exercise program for plantar fasciitis was non-inferior to hospital physiotherapy for 3-month first-step morning pain and less costly from both payer (-¥4,920) and societal (-¥7,008) perspectives.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation and Individualized Physical Therapy on Pain and Function in Individuals With Chronic Knee Pain: A Pilot Study.
item.description: A pilot study with 30 participants found that active tDCS combined with individualized PT showed no significant differences in primary patient-centered pain and functional outcomes for chronic knee pain compared to sham tDCS, though improvements in pain sensitivity and quadriceps strength were observed for secondary outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Load-dependent Motor Cortical Activation Assessed by fNIRS Is Partially Preserved After Stroke.
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 12 stroke patients found that proportional load-dependent hemodynamic cortical responses during upper limb lifting tasks were preserved only in the ipsilesional posterior parietal cortex, unlike healthy controls who showed responses in multiple motor areas.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Adapted cardiac rehabilitation for individuals after stroke and transient ischaemic attack: A scoping review.
item.description: A scoping review of 19 studies (1951 participants) found that adapted cardiac rehabilitation for individuals after stroke and TIA is safe, feasible, and acceptable, though evidence for effectiveness and inclusion of those with moderate to severe disability is limited.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of a soft robotic exoskeleton for upper-limb rehabilitation in subacute stroke inpatient rehabilitation: a randomised controlled trial
item.description: This randomized controlled trial investigates the efficacy of a soft robotic exoskeleton for upper-limb rehabilitation in subacute stroke inpatient rehabilitation.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: Ideal Versus Actual School-Based Physiotherapy Practice in Israel: A National Survey.
item.description: A national survey (n=202 actual, n=152 ideal) comparing actual and ideal school-based physiotherapy practice in Israel found significant gaps in 25 of 30 items. Actual practice showed lower frequencies of collaborative, consultative, and participation-oriented activities, with barriers including team dynamics, resources, and administrative support.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Patient-reported knee osteoarthritis problems and rehabilitation goals: A qualitative study.
item.description: A qualitative study of 387 participants with knee osteoarthritis found that patients identified wide-ranging knee problems, including impairments, activity limitations, and participation restrictions, with diverse 3-month rehabilitation goals often centered on high-level physical activities.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Music-based interventions in adult stroke rehabilitation: a narrative review of clinical applications, proposed mechanisms, and implementation.
item.description: A narrative review on music-based interventions in adult stroke rehabilitation found consistent evidence for rhythmic auditory stimulation in gait and music-supported upper-limb programs, with potential for melodic intonation therapy in nonfluent aphasia, but highlights inconsistent terminology and overstated mechanisms.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of an Integrated Treatment of Vestibular Rehabilitation and Cognitive Behavior Therapy for Chronic Dizziness in a Community-Based Population: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A single-blinded RCT (n=105) found no statistically significant between-group differences in dizziness-related handicap or gait speed at 6 or 12 months when comparing integrated vestibular rehabilitation and cognitive behavioral strategies (VR-CBT) with a brief vestibular intervention (BI-VR) in community-based adults with chronic dizziness.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Balancing Offloading and Comfort: The Effect of Forefoot Rocker Curvature on In-Shoe Plantar Pressure and Gait Kinematics
item.description: A study in 10 healthy adults found that a straight-line rocker profile (CRi) significantly reduced metatarsal head pressure (mean pressure=80 kPa) compared to curved rockers, but was perceived as least comfortable and affected ankle dorsiflexion. Rocker curvature is a key design parameter for therapeutic footwear.
item.author: medRxiv
